title: Private Data And Planning Memory Ingestion Roadmap

format_decision.reason: The plan must be visible in Roadmap Lens and claimable by PlanRuntime, but runtime transfer/indexing state must not be stored in monolithic planning JSON.

goal: Make Odysseus ingest its planning documents and a 100GB+ private Nextcloud corpus into durable, resumable, provenance-aware memory on the homeserver without raw-content leaks or fragile one-shot jobs.

done_definition.feature_done_means: Implemented, focused tests green, committed, pushed, live-installed on the server, and verified through live health/API checks.
final_goal_reached_when: All repo planning sources under specs/roadmaps and docs/plans are discoverable as memory sources with stable IDs and provenance.
Planning-source memory ingestion is incremental and updates changed/deleted/renamed plan files without duplicate memory.
A 100GB+ Nextcloud source can be inventoried, transferred or mounted, scanned, analyzed, retried, and resumed after interruption.
Operational transfer and analysis state lives in a resumable ledger such as SQLite or an append-only event log, not in a giant JSON document.
Large-file analysis uses chunked streaming and bounded extraction lanes.
Memory writes store abstractions, hashes, provenance, and sidecar references, not raw private file bodies by default.
The live server exposes status, progress, stuck-item recovery, retry, pause/resume, and evidence for the ingestion pipeline.

existing_building_blocks: scripts/agent_migration_manifest.py can build read-only manifests from source exports.
src/nextcloud_source_provider.py models offline Nextcloud source readiness.
src/nextcloud_intake_ledger.py defines redacted per-file intake ledger entries.
src/universal_inbox_pipeline.py and related universal_inbox modules model extraction, routing, placement, policy, memory abstraction, and write gates.
src/embedding_lanes.py and tests cover resumable lane backfill behavior.
src/memory_perf_suite_runner.py and tests cover checkpoint/recovery patterns for memory workloads.
ops/homeserver/nextcloud-podman contains homeserver Nextcloud deployment assets.
known_gaps: No single Big Data Runner currently owns 100GB+ transfer, inventory, extraction, indexing, retry, resume, and status.
Planning documents are plentiful but not guaranteed to flow into bounded memory context.
Live Nextcloud access and writes remain gated and must not be assumed.
A monolithic JSON manifest is unsuitable as the operational source of truth for 100GB+ scans.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use JSON roadmaps for planning only. Use SQLite or append-only event logs for transfer and analysis checkpoints.
architecture_decisions.why: 100GB+ file sets need frequent checkpoint writes, range queries, retries, stuck-item detection, and crash-safe updates.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use compact manifests for immutable snapshots and a ledger for mutable job state.
architecture_decisions.why: A manifest proves what existed; a ledger proves what was attempted, failed, retried, skipped, or indexed.

architecture_decisions.decision: Separate transfer/mirror verification from content analysis.
architecture_decisions.why: A transfer failure should not corrupt the memory index, and an extraction failure should not imply file loss.

architecture_decisions.decision: Store summaries, derived facts, hashes, MIME metadata, source refs, and graph edges by default; keep raw content in source files.
architecture_decisions.why: Odysseus memory should be useful without becoming an uncontrolled duplicate of private data.

non_goals: No destructive Nextcloud sync or delete operation in the first live track.
No automatic write of new Nextcloud tags until tag governance and operator approval are live.
No provider calls over the entire 100GB corpus before local extraction, sampling, and budget gates pass.
No giant JSON dump of file contents, embeddings, or operational state.
No direct mutation of existing private files during inventory or analysis.
stop_rules: Stop on secrets, tokens, credentials, chat IDs, or private raw content being logged into repo files or roadmap evidence.
Stop if a transfer command would delete, overwrite, move, or chmod private data without explicit operator approval.
Stop if the homeserver target path, Nextcloud data path, user/owner mapping, or available disk budget is ambiguous.
Stop if a scan cannot resume from checkpoint after forced interruption.
Stop if memory ingestion stores raw private bodies instead of bounded abstractions and provenance.
Stop if live server health, Chroma heartbeat, or ingestion status route fails after deployment.
Stop if throughput tests imply the full corpus would run unbounded or starve the main Odysseus service.

version_horizons.target: Planning docs enter memory and large-data ingestion has a safe dry-run ledger.

version_horizons.label: 0.10 Transfer

version_horizons.label: 0.11 Analysis

Proof that planning docs can be re-indexed incrementally without duplicate memory.

verification: Focused tests for source inventory, stable IDs, changed-file detection, and redaction.
No file contents over configured preview budget in artifacts.

graph_nodes.title: Big Data ledger contract
deliverables: Operational ledger schema for file inventory, transfer state, extraction state, analysis state, retries, and errors.
Checkpoint semantics for resume, pause, retry, skip, and stale lock recovery.
Privacy contract: metadata and hashes only unless explicitly scoped.

abc.reason: The ledger is core infrastructure and must be testable offline before touching live data.

verification: Focused recovery tests simulate interruption and resume.
Ledger rejects raw content and secret-like fields.
Large synthetic inventory test stays bounded.

graph_nodes.title: Nextcloud transfer readiness
deliverables: Operator-reviewed transfer plan for 100GB+ Nextcloud data to homeserver.
Decision between local Nextcloud sync path, rclone/WebDAV, rsync over SSH, or server-side copy.
No-delete first-run policy with checksum/size verification.

abc.reason: Operator runbook and Go/No-Go wording must be exact before any live transfer.

verification: Readiness check has no missing source/target/disk/permission inputs.
Dry-run command is recorded without credentials.
No live transfer starts until explicit operator Go.

graph_nodes.title: Resumable transfer tooling
deliverables: Scripted transfer wrapper for the chosen tool with dry-run, copy-only, resume, verify, and log modes.
Ledger records per-file status without raw content.
A forced interruption test proves resume without re-copying completed files.

abc.reason: Transfer wrapper and tests can be built offline with fake directories before live use.

verification: Focused tests with synthetic nested files and large sparse/fake files.
Dry-run produces no file mutation.
Interrupted run resumes from ledger state.

graph_nodes.title: Resumable scanner dry-run
deliverables: Filesystem scanner can process large trees in pages/batches.
Scanner records inode/path/hash/size/mtime state and resumes after interruption.
Unsupported, denied, too-large, and unstable files become recoverable ledger states.

abc.reason: Scanner resilience is testable before live transfer or analysis.

verification: Focused scanner tests with thousands of synthetic files.
Forced interruption then resume reaches stable complete state.
Memory usage remains bounded by batch size.

graph_nodes.title: Live small-batch transfer
deliverables: A small representative subset transfers to the homeserver and verifies successfully.
Ledger records live evidence, duration, bytes, file count, skipped files, failures, and retry state.
No destructive operation is used.

abc.reason: First live transfer requires operator Go, integration, health checks, and evidence.

verification: Live transfer subset completes and verifies.
GET /api/health and Chroma heartbeat pass after run.
Resume command is tested on the same subset without duplicate writes.

graph_nodes.title: Chunked extraction lanes
deliverables: Extraction lanes process supported file types incrementally.
Large files are chunked, skipped, or queued according to explicit policy.
Failures are retryable and do not block unrelated files.

abc.reason: Extraction and lane behavior need focused offline tests before live corpus analysis.

verification: Focused extraction and embedding lane tests.
Synthetic large-file test proves bounded memory and resumability.
Unsupported file types become ledger states, not crashes.

graph_nodes.title: Memory abstraction ingest live
deliverables: Analyzed files produce durable memory abstractions with provenance.
Duplicate or changed files update memory by digest/source ref instead of creating blind duplicates.
RAPTOR/derived graph write gates are respected.

abc.reason: Memory correctness needs integration with the active memory gates and live verification.

verification: Focused universal inbox memory/pipeline/write-gate tests.
Live probe shows memory item source refs for a small approved batch.
Raw-content leak tests pass.

graph_nodes.title: Full 100GB+ transfer live
deliverables: Full source corpus is copied or mirrored to homeserver in copy-only/resumable mode.
Verification report covers file counts, byte counts, skipped paths, failures, and retry plan.
Partial failure can be resumed without starting over.

abc.reason: The full live transfer is a high-impact operator-gated action.

verification: Live transfer status reaches complete or partial-with-retry-plan.
Resume after interruption works.
No source files are deleted or mutated.

graph_nodes.title: Full corpus analysis live
deliverables: The full corpus is analyzed incrementally with progress and recovery.
Failures are isolated to individual items and can be retried.
Memory/graph output remains bounded, deduped, and provenance-aware.

abc.reason: Full corpus analysis must be live-managed and stopped safely if resource gates trip.

verification: Live pipeline status reports total, completed, failed, skipped, retryable, and throughput.
Forced pause/resume works.
Health checks remain green during and after analysis.

graph_nodes.title: Ingestion dashboard live
deliverables: Operator can see transfer, scan, extraction, memory ingest, failures, retry queue, and throughput.
Controls are permission-gated and do not allow accidental destructive actions.
Dashboard links evidence back to source refs and roadmap nodes.

abc.reason: After backend status exists, frontend can expose operational controls safely.

verification: Focused frontend/static tests if available.
Live UI smoke test for dashboard status.
Controls remain disabled unless policy gate allows them.

plan_graph_projection.edge_policy: Dependencies define claimability. Live transfer, live analysis, Nextcloud access, and memory writes also require explicit operator Go even when dependencies are complete.

next_actions.action: Implement the resumable metadata-only operational ledger contract for large private-data ingestion.
Collect operator inputs for source path, target path, disk budget, transfer tool, and dry-run command after ledger contract is live.
Build a resumable scanner dry-run after the ledger contract exists.

roles.alice: Operator runbooks, Go/No-Go language, live transfer input checklist, policy wording.
roles.bob: Offline models, scripts, scanner/ledger/extraction tests, dashboard slices.
roles.charlie: Integration, live gates, commits, pushes, deploys, status checks, evidence, high-impact live actions.

parallelism_policy: Planning source inventory and Big Data ledger contract may run in parallel if files do not overlap.
No live Nextcloud transfer before readiness and transfer tooling are complete.
No full-corpus analysis before small-batch live transfer and memory abstraction ingest are verified.
Exactly one live-impacting action runs at a time.
After each live-installed feature, update this roadmap evidence before selecting the next claimable node.

per_feature_sequence: Check git status and stop on foreign staged files or hotfile conflicts.
Update this roadmap completion_state with commit and live evidence.
Commit/push the evidence update and install it live before starting the next feature.
